current_answer: As of 13 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. But “not broadly worse” no longer means “nothing changed”: OpenAI documents a narrow GPT-6 Astra monitorability loss relative to GPT-5.6 Sol, and its guidance says context, skills, and completion boundaries can alter Astra’s behavior. A new Codex report adds adjacent-turn intent loss; another reports a 14% to 88% server-meter jump beside 98.1% cached local input. Snorkel’s 66-task Terminal-Bench places Astra and Fable 5.1 close at the top, a counterweight to collapse claims. Current status pages show OpenAI, Google Cloud, and Grok operational, while Claude Cowork remains degraded on Windows. Specific model-behavior, context, tool, product, and account-surface failures are real; broad weight decline remains unproven. Audit context and trace the final model, tool lifecycle, artifact, and allowance before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad core-capability decline is proven. But Astra has a documented monitorability regression, context-sensitive guidance, and fresh Codex agent/account failure reports, while an independent 66-task benchmark is a counterweight. Test the surface and trace before you switch.

summary: OpenAI’s Astra system card reports lower written-chain-of-thought monitorability than GPT-5.6 Sol in oversight-oriented evaluations while reporting stronger capabilities and alignment. That is a narrow model property, not a user-task quality score; the finding is largely adversarial and provider-authored.

OpenAI’s 11 September guidance says long or contradictory skills, AGENTS.md files, and prompts can crowd context, overconstrain Astra, trigger an early stop, reduce delegation, or expand testing. This is a real comparison variable when a workflow changes after a model update.

A 9 September Codex issue reports adjacent-turn intent loss, drift from an established reporting skill, and ineffective corrections on Astra. It is detailed but one self-selected workflow with no independent fresh-environment reproduction.

A separate Codex issue reports a server-provided weekly meter jumping from 14% to 88% used in one response. The associated record shows 200,123 total tokens; 98.1% of 55.3 million local input tokens across 232 responses was cached. This needs server reconciliation, not a billing verdict.

Terminal-Bench 4.0 reports Astra 58.2% ±2.8 and Fable 5.1 57.9% ±3.8 on a 66-task Harbor run; Sol is 37.3% ±3.8. Different agents, effort settings, costs, and the cross-sectional design make it a counterweight, not a longitudinal stability test.

Current status pages report OpenAI, Google Cloud, and Grok operational or without a broad severe incident. Claude Cowork is the exception: degraded on Windows while claude.ai, Console, Claude API, and Claude Code are operational.

Reader move: audit loaded context and completion boundaries; record visible and effective model, surface, route, runtime, tool lifecycle, final artifact, objective preservation, retries, tokens, allowance, time, and cost before switching.
uncertainty: The Astra monitorability result concerns oversight and adversarial evaluation, not ordinary task quality; OpenAI is the source and notes that absence of observed failures does not prove reliability.
The Codex intent and meter reports are single self-selected reports. Independent replay, causal attribution, and the provider’s allowance ledger are absent.
Terminal-Bench is cross-sectional and harness-dependent; Snorkel discloses its grant support and reviewer role.
Status pages are aggregate snapshots and do not test individual accounts, routes, tasks, or final artifacts.
No public matched longitudinal cross-provider capability series, independent Astra replay, or first-party audience analytics is available.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source check completed 13 September 2026. The new evidence sharpens a narrow Astra model-property lane and context confounder; provider status, issue reports, benchmark scores, and account telemetry remain dated snapshots with explicit scope limits.
